Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together.
Your application must include the following:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, please provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume. Please include an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa - for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
If you have them, please include the following:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard however it could strengthen your application in circumstances such as explaining a gap in your education or if your education/degree subject is not directly related to the programme. The personal statement should be no more than one side of A4 and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
Documents which are not required:
- References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases we may request a reference to help us make a decision.
Applicants with Indian degrees should include:
- A copy of your bachelor's degree certificate.
- A copy of your consolidated mark sheet.
- A copy of your semester mark sheets.
- A copy of your University marking scheme.
- Official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%).
Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal as this will link the document to the correct application automatically.

Interview Requirements.content: We aim to make decisions within **three to five weeks** if all necessary documents have been received. You will be contacted directly if we require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview or audition. You will receive an email asking you to check your applicant portal for more details.

Application Deadlines.content:
Start date: **September 2026**
**Application deadlines**
- **31 July 2026** – International applicants
- **11 September 2026** – UK applicants
Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible. International students are recommended to apply as early as possible to ensure that they have time to apply for their visa.

Academic Requirements.content:
A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons)** in a subject including, but not limited to, geography, urban planning, engineering, land resource, statistics, data science, information management, transport or computer science, where quantitative and/or computing skills can be evidenced. Alternative subjects which may be considered include, but are not limited to, architecture, finance, mathematics or psychology. All applicants should possess an interest in using data science to tackle real-life urban challenges.
Applicants with a **2:2 (hons)** will be considered on a case-by-case basis where they can demonstrate relevant work experience or competence in a relevant specialist field. Professional qualifications and relevant experience can also be considered.
International applicants: The University accepts a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications).
Applicants from China: accepted postgraduate qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. Applicants should check that their institution is accepted and that they meet the entry requirements before making an application. If the programme asks for **2.1**, applicants from China need **70%-85%, depending on institution**. If the programme asks for **2.2**, applicants from China need **70%-80%, depending on institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
IELTS **6.5 overall**, with **no less than 6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Options include [Language for Science (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i204/language-for-science), [Language for Science: General Science (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i203/language-for-science-general-science), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).

Program Overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: on campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
Urban data science and analytics are critical to helping cities evolve, providing insight into urban processes, dynamics within cities, and local and global issues. The Urban Data Science and Analytics MSc offers the opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge of the methods and approaches of data science and learn how to apply them in understanding cities and setting urban policy. The course combines technical training in the latest data science techniques, from data wrangling to machine learning, visualisation, and beyond, with the critical thinking needed to interrogate and understand complex urban and mobility challenges.
At the heart of this course is a commitment to tackling real-world challenges facing cities. Researchers at the University of Leeds are finding novel data-driven solutions to challenges such as traffic congestion, social and economic equality, healthy cities, and competition for resources. Graduates are intended to be equipped with the experience, technical skills, and knowledge needed to pursue careers in areas such as data science, software development, or urban planning.
Why study at Leeds:
- Learn the latest innovations in critical areas of urban analytics with exposure to impactful research across the [School of Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research), the [Institute for Transport Studies](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/transport-research), the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the national institute for data science and artificial intelligence which feeds directly into the course.
- Advance skills and knowledge in key topics sought after in industry, including programming for data science, creative coding for urban problems and analytics for urban policy.
- Tailor the course to career aspirations with optional study in areas like geographic data visualisation, geodemographics and transport data science.
- Conduct project work to develop transferable research skills, investigating a real-world issue that explores and develops individual interests.
- Access specialist facilities including research-grade laboratories in the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and a GIS computer cluster with industry-standard software.
- Experience theoretical and practical teaching delivered by academics actively engaged in research and part of the [Institute for Spatial Data Science](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research-centre-spatial-analysis-policy), [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/collaborate-turing/current-partnerships-and-collaborations/university-leeds).
- Build industry connections through working with external organisations and stakeholders, co-developing creative solutions to urban problems.
- Put theory into practice with fieldwork opportunities in an urban context, observing how data science can be used to create and shape urban policy and how policies impact urban systems and processes.
The course combines technical training in data science with a rich exploration of urban systems and policy, enabling students to create novel data analyses informed by a contextual understanding of cities. The first term introduces the theory and application of urban data science through complementary study of data science applications, urban analysis, and programming. The second term builds and expands this knowledge through urban policy analytics, field trips, creative problem-solving, group work with industry experts, and optional deeper training in spatial analysis or transport.
Over the summer months students complete a 60-credit dissertation-style research project, bringing together learning from each module and producing a documented code workbook with a supporting 5000-word practical briefing. The project focuses on how data science methods can inform policy interventions and decision-making, allows students to apply learning to a real-world problem, and may include the opportunity to work with industry partners. Example dissertation themes include urban economics, cities and crime, urban inequalities, transport and mobility, housing and real estate, health and wellbeing, smart cities, pollution, vulnerable populations, geodemographics, and fieldwork.
Field courses provide opportunities to explore urban analytics on the ground in urban environments. Students consider cities from different perspectives, observe urban systems across policy areas, collect data, make observations and assessments, and explore cities in new ways.
The course incorporates innovative modes of delivery with a focus on practical, problem-based learning. Face-to-face learning in workshops, small groups, drop-ins, laboratories, lectures, and seminars is combined with teaching and learning delivered using interactive digital platforms. Students are taught by an experienced team of academics and researchers actively engaged in cutting-edge research and part of the [Institute for Spatial Data Science](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research-centre-spatial-analysis-policy), [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/), and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/). Teaching may also be delivered by industry professionals and trained postgraduate researchers.
Assessment is primarily through the production of code and critical analysis for the exploration of urban phenomena and problems. Some modules focus more on qualitative analysis of urban systems, while others incorporate team-based assessment. Code and analyses through a personal protected GitHub repository are documented and act as a portfolio of work for future employers.
This course is taught by the [School of Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography), [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing), and [Institute for Transport Studies](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/transport).
Career opportunities: the course teaches in-depth technical knowledge and skills in data science along with training in workflow practice, teamwork, and “hacking” sought by employers. Students also build an online portfolio of work developed throughout the course to demonstrate skills to prospective employers. On completion, graduates have the technical knowledge to secure employment in local government, companies handling spatial data, start-ups, transportation authorities and operators, urban planners and consultancies such as Arup and Mott MacDonald, in roles such as data scientist, data analyst or software developer. Previous students on this course have secured positions including Data Analytics at Amey, Graduate Scheme at Ernst & Young, and Data Science Internships at LIDA.
Work placements and industry experience: Masters students at Leeds have the opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with the Global Industry Programme, developing professional skills and gaining insight into working in their chosen field by solving a real business problem from a live company brief. The programme is fully online and designed to fit around studies, offers professional networking opportunities, builds consultancy experience with a UK or international organisation, involves team work across disciplines, and helps students put course teaching into practice.

Curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The course combines technical training in data science with a rich exploration of urban systems and policy, enabling you to create novel data analyses that are informed by a contextual understanding of cities.
- Semester 1: Data Science for Practical Applications; Analysing Cities; Programming for Spatial Data Science.
- Semester 2: Analytics for Urban Policy; Creative Coding for Real-World Problems; optional modules incorporating deeper training in spatial analysis or transport training.
[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Urban Data Science and Analytics MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-UDS%26A-FT).
Compulsory modules:
- **Programming for Spatial Data Science – 15 credits**
- **Data Science for Practical Applications – 15 credits**
- **Creative Coding for Real-World Problems – 15 credits**
- **Analysing Cities – 15 credits**
- **Analytics for Urban Policy – 30 credits**
- **Urban Data Science Project – 60 credits**: over the summer months you'll work on a 60-credit dissertation-style research project, producing a documented code workbook with a supporting 5000-word practical briefing. You'll also have the opportunity to work with industry partners on this project.
Example dissertation themes for Urban Data Science and Analytics MSc include:
- Urban economics
- Cities and crime
- Urban inequalities
- Transport and mobility
- Housing and real estate
- Health and wellbeing
- Smart cities
- Pollution
- Vulnerable populations
- Geodemographics
- Fieldwork
Optional modules are indicative of typical options:
- **Geographic Data Visualisation & Analysis – 15 credits**
- **Geodemographics and Neighbourhood Analysis – 15 credits**
- **Transport Data Collection and Analysis – 15 credits**
- **Transport Data Science – 15 credits**
Field courses provide students an opportunity to explore urban analytics ‘on the ground’ in inspiring urban environments, with a chance to collect data, make observations and assessments, and explore cities.
The course incorporates workshops, small groups, drop-ins, laboratories, lectures, and seminars, combined with teaching and learning delivered using interactive digital platforms. The ‘Creative Coding’ module focuses on problem-based learning, where you'll work with other students in teams to tackle problems and datasets provided by external stakeholders.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The information is provided as a guideline only, based on average spending. The following estimates are for a single student in 2025 based on the latest data available; actual amount will depend on accommodation type and availability, and lifestyle. They don’t include tuition fees.
| Cost category | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |
| Household bills: gas and/or electricity, water and broadband internet (included in most university accommodation and some private accommodation) | £14 to £17 |
| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Please note that we do not permit deferrals.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
A conditional offer from the University of Leeds means you need to achieve the grades or points outlined in your offer letter. The offer letter will also explain any English language requirements, if applicable.
- If you have an academic offer condition, the University may need to see your degree certificate and transcripts as evidence.
- If you have an English language condition, you may be able to meet the requirements by taking a [pre-sessional course at the Language Centre](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english).
- You can upload evidence that you have met your conditions and accept your offer in the [application portal](https://myleedsportal.leeds.ac.uk/signin-landing/).
- You may have to accept your offer again if it becomes unconditional.
- If your offer has an academic condition, you will need to include official translations alongside your final academic documents if they were not originally produced in English.
- If you take a [pre-sessional English course](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english) with the Language Centre to meet your language condition, you may be eligible for a combined offer. This means that when you pass your pre-sessional, and have met any conditions in your offer letter, you are automatically enrolled on your degree course.
